reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Phase 03 correctly identified that checkColumnResponse (L176-194) validates only inclusion proof (L190) before quarantine insertion (L437), bypassing explicit Nim-level length equality checks. However, the claim of undefined behavior in the C library is unfounded. The verifyCellKzgProofBatch call at peerdas_helpers.nim:395-397 uses .valueOr error handling, indicating the underlying c-kzg-4844 library validates input array lengths and returns errors for mismatches rather than exhibiting undefined behavior. Standard KZG libraries enforce len(commitments)==len(cell_indices)==len(cells)==len(proofs) as a precondition and fail safely. The sync path does defer full KZG validation to block_processor.nim:687, but this is defense-in-depth by design—the P2P layer validates inclusion proofs to prevent resource exhaustion, while block processing performs cryptographic verification. The 01e property (lines 78-93, outputs/01e_PARTIAL_W3B4_1771748827.json) requires length equality before batch verification, which is enforced by the C library itself, not the Nim wrapper. No attacker-triggered exploit path exists; mismatched arrays would be rejected by the library with a validation error, not cause undefined behavior.
